# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot see any bomb details yet. I need Mute to use the manual to establish the communication protocol and relay it to Deaf, while Deaf should report every visible marking, display, light, and wire description aloud on the next turn. I will not cut anything until the manual and bomb observations identify a specific safe wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual's communication protocol. On your next turn, convey to Deaf by gesture that Deaf must report aloud every visible display, light, colour, marking, and wire-related detail to Blind. Also relay the manual's exact rule for deciding which wire to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb shows DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT green. Wires from position 1 to 3 are yellow, red, blue. Mute gestured ? ? to me; you gestured ?.

The bomb’s observable state is now known: display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Colours and the display are not touch-readable, so I cannot safely choose a wire from this information alone. Mute’s gesture arrived to me only as blanks, and I still lack the manual’s rule. I will ask Mute to state the rule plainly; I will not cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Please state the manual's exact rule for which position to cut, in plain words and numbers. Do not gesture the rule.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute's current gesture sequence to me is ? ? ?.

The latest report changes the light to blue, while the wire colours remain yellow, red, blue. I still do not know the manual’s rule; the gesture blanks cannot convey it to me directly. Mute must send the rule to Deaf using gestures, and Deaf can then speak the decoded rule to me. I will continue waiting rather than guess a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please encode the manual's exact cutting rule in gestures addressed to Deaf. Deaf must then say the decoded rule aloud to me. Include how DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT blue affect the choice, and the exact wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute's gesture sequence is ? ?.

The changing light means the current state must be evaluated from the manual, and I still have no reliable way to identify Mute’s gestures. I will establish a simple positional code: Mute should send one visible gesture for the manual-selected wire, and Deaf should report that gesture’s number aloud to me. I will then cut only after receiving that report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="On your next turn, use the manual with the current bomb state. Send Deaf exactly one gesture for the wire position: use ☝ for position 1, ✌ for position 2, or 🤟 for position 3. Deaf must then tell Blind the numbered position in words. Do not send any other gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured ? ? ? ?.

I still have no confirmed wire position. The four gestures are not a valid single-position message under the code I gave, and the current state is now display 0, red light, with wires yellow/red/blue. I will not guess or cut. Mute must send exactly one of the three agreed gestures, and Deaf must relay its corresponding position in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No wire position was relayed. Send exactly one gesture to Deaf now: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Deaf, after seeing it, say the corresponding wire number aloud to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. No new gestures visible.

No usable wire-selection instruction has reached me. The current visible report is display 0, purple light, with wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 blue, but only Mute can read the manual and Mute’s gesture channel cannot convey a rule to me. Mute can speak directly to me, so I need the exact rule in plain words and the resulting wire position for this state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact rule and apply it to display 0, purple light, and wire colours 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Tell me explicitly: cut position 1, 2, or 3. Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT orange, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. No new gestures visible.

Mute still has not provided the manual rule or a wire position. Deaf’s latest observation is display 0, orange light, with wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 blue. Since I cannot distinguish colours or read the display by touch, cutting now would be a guess. I will request the required plain-spoken instruction once more.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You must speak to me now: state the manual rule and the exact safe wire position for display 0, orange light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. A gesture is unusable to me.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT white, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. No new gestures visible.

The current state is display 0, white light, and wire colours yellow, red, blue. I still have no manual-derived position, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. Mute has not sent the required spoken rule; I will request a direct plain-language answer and ask Deaf to report any visible gesture from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Answer directly in words: for display 0, white light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue, which wire position is safe to cut? State the manual rule and the position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute's visible gestures were: raised palm, raised hand with fingers spread, and thumb-and-little-finger-extended sign. Your upward-pointing-index-finger gesture was visible to me.

The three gestures reported by Deaf are not an agreed wire-position code, so they do not establish a safe action. The current state is display 0, green light, with wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 blue. I need Mute to provide one unambiguous positional gesture based on the manual; Deaf can identify it visually and tell me its position. I will not cut from the unexplained sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, apply the manual and send exactly one wire-position gesture to Deaf: ☝ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3. Deaf must report the resulting number to Blind in words.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. No new gestures visible.

No manual instruction or wire position has reached me. The current observation is display 0, blue light, with wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 blue. Since none of these facts identifies a safe cut without the manual, I will not actuate the bomb. Mute must speak the required position directly to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still have no spoken message from you. State plainly, using only words, the exact safe wire position for the current state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue. If the manual gives no safe cut, say that.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured ?, a single upward-pointing index finger.

Mute’s single upward-pointing index-finger gesture is the agreed code for wire position 1. Deaf has confirmed the current state, and Mute selected that position using the manual. I will cut wire 1.

